why: Counting pairs by value needs an index per value, but values span 2^32: coordinate compression maps them to ranks 1..m first, and then a Fenwick tree counts, for each element scanned from the right, how many smaller values are already to its right.
hints: An inversion is a later smaller value. Scanning from the right, what do you need to know about the values already seen?
You need 'how many seen values are smaller than v', a prefix count over values. Values are huge, so replace each by its rank among the sorted distinct values.
Scan right to left: add the Fenwick prefix count of ranks below rank(v), then insert rank(v). O(n log n). (Merge sort counting also works.)
pitfalls: Equal values are not inversions: count strictly smaller ranks.
Do not index an array by raw values up to 2^31.
